consensus_summary: The biblical fool primarily symbolizes moral-spiritual rebellion or practical godlessness (rejecting God/divine wisdom and living accordingly), not intellectual deficiency; a settled core across sources, with secondary notes on Hebrew gradations, the Pauline 'fool for Christ' inversion, and insult usage.
book_summary: The fool is one who hears God's word and will not do it—the lawless, not the unintelligent; opposite of the wise.
consensus_core_identification: morally/spiritually rebellious person who rejects God or divine wisdom (practical godlessness), not the unintelligent
book_core_identification: hearer of God's word who will not do it (the lawless, not the unintelligent)
boundary_disagreement: Book centers the category on the non-obedient hearer of the word (Matt 7:26 type), while consensus primary extends more broadly to practical atheism, despising instruction, self-trust, corruption, and unpreparedness without requiring prior hearing of the word.
rationale: Minimum cores share the same referent category (moral-spiritual failure re: God, explicitly not low intelligence) and the same opposite (wise). The book does not replace that referent; it preserves it while tightening the defining condition and extension to the lawless non-doer of heard word. This excludes or de-emphasizes some consensus-admitted cases (e.g., pure practical atheism or hardened scorner without the hearing-not-doing frame) without contradicting the center, yielding refinement by narrowing rather than divergence or novelty.
strongest_objection: Psalm 14:1 (explicitly cited) paradigmatically frames the fool as one who says there is no God and acts corruptly, a broader practical-atheism sense that the book's 'hears and will not do' formulation does not fully capture.
